title: Module adjunction unit isomorphism for an isomorphic scheme map
statement: For an isomorphism of schemes, the underlying additive sheaf map of the canonical module adjunction unit is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Set R and S to the completed commutative coefficient sheaves on Y and X, and c to the specified completed inverse-image coefficient isomorphism. By proEtaleIsoInverseImage_equivalence, the sheaf inverse image along g is an equivalence. Its adjunction unit is therefore invertible. The coefficient direct-image map is this unit followed by the direct image of c.hom, so is invertible; forgetting commutativity preserves its invertibility.

proof.text: Apply the already proved isoModulePushforwardEquivalence in ProEtaleIsomorphismInverseImage to the ring sheaves underlying R and S and this invertible coefficient direct-image map. Its forward functor is definitionally proEtaleRingModuleDirectImage g R S c: the site functor is base change and the scalar map is the same adjoint coefficient map. Thus the actual module direct-image functor is an equivalence. This reuses the general, proved helper, not only the constant-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: Mathlib Adjunction.instIsIsoFunctorUnitOfIsEquivalence makes the unit of the actual normalized proEtaleRingModuleAdjunction an isomorphism because its right adjoint is an equivalence. Take its component at purTwistIntegralModule Y l E and apply the underlying additive sheaf functor, which preserves isomorphisms. This is exactly the asserted map.
